## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Verdict | Confirmed recovery-path correctness gap |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium |
| Task Type | Targeted workflow safety fix with regression coverage |

### What Was Claimed

After a durable merge succeeds, post-merge work runs before the merged workflow label is projected. If that work fails, the run can remain projected as `workflow:awaiting-merge` even though the pull request is merged.

### What We Found

The ordinary finalization path in the current integration tree already records the merge effect and completed merge phase, then projects `workflow:merged` before `postReviewCompletionArtifacts`. The dispatcher-owned merge path also attempts the merged projection before its post-merge artifacts.

A recovery path still violates the same contract. `#recoverDirectTerminal` accepts durable merge evidence, validates the merged pull request, then performs cleanup, terminal journal writes, and terminal projection before calling `#projectWorkflowStage(link, "merged", ...)`. Any failure in cleanup or terminal work can therefore leave the issue carrying `workflow:awaiting-merge` after a durable merge.

### Root Cause

Merged projection ordering is enforced in normal finalization but not consistently at the durable-merge recovery boundary. The recovery method treats cleanup and terminal artifact work as prerequisites to the merged projection even though those operations are independent, throwable post-merge effects.

### Affected Files

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — move recovery-path merged projection ahead of cleanup and centralize the ordering contract.
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` — add focused failure/order regression coverage.

### Evidence

- In `#finalize`, the merge effect and merge phase completion are durable before the merged projection and review completion artifacts.
- In dispatcher merge handling, the merged projection is attempted immediately after the merge effect and before `postReviewCompletionArtifacts`.
- In `#recoverDirectTerminal`, `github.deleteBranch`, `#git.cleanup`, terminal journal appends, and terminal event projection precede the current merged projection.
- `#recoverDirectTerminal` is reached from restart reconciliation when merge and close evidence are durable; its post-merge operations can throw before the late label call.
- Existing tests assert `workflowLabelForNode("merge", "merged")` and durable merge evidence but do not exercise ordering when post-merge work throws.

### History Findings

The issue references review finding `workflow-correctness-001` from PR #117. The current tree appears to contain an earlier normal-path ordering correction, but the recovery-path ordering remains unprotected. No additional repository history was required or available through the bounded read-only inspection tools.

### Recommendation

Project `workflow:merged` immediately after durable merge evidence is established in `#recoverDirectTerminal`, before cleanup, terminal artifacts, or lease-release projection. Use a small async ordering helper in all merge completion paths so a regression test can prove the merged projection runs before a failing post-merge callback.

### Related Issues

- Source review finding: `workflow-correctness-001` from PR #117.
- Issue #119: durable merged state must not remain projected as awaiting merge.

### Decomposition Assessment

Single-concern change. No decomposition is necessary; scope is limited to merge projection ordering and focused tests.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Durable merge evidence is followed by `workflow:merged` projection before recovery cleanup and terminal artifacts.
- [ ] Normal and dispatcher merge paths retain the same ordering contract.
- [ ] A focused regression test proves projection precedes a failing post-merge operation.
- [ ] `check` passes and the exact remediation head receives fresh correctness and security review.
